title: Radiological Manifestations of Invasive Fungal Infections in Emergency Settings: A Comprehensive Review
content: Invasive fungal infections can present with rapidly progressive tissue injury before microbiological confirmation is available. Emergency imaging must identify the affected organ, detect complications and guide further diagnostic assessment. This narrative review synthesizes selected imaging studies and consensus guidance on computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging and ultrasonography in adult emergency and acute-care settings. Findings are interpreted according to fungal biology, host immune status and disease timing. Pulmonary manifestations include angioinvasive and airway-predominant patterns; sinonasal assessment emphasizes extrasinus extension, tissue viability and orbital or intracranial complications. Central nervous system imaging addresses abscesses, infarction and haemorrhage, while abdominal and urinary assessment identifies visceral lesions, bowel compromise and obstruction. Critical appraisal of selected studies highlights limitations related to patient selection, small samples, reference standards and transferability of diagnostic estimates. The review connects these findings to examination selection, vascular assessment, urgent communication and sampling targets through a proposed clinical workflow. Imaging supports suspicion and defines disease extent but cannot independently establish fungal aetiology. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether integrated imaging pathways improve diagnostic timing and patient outcomes.
